title: Edge-on galaxy hosts supernova explosion
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy IC 755, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IC 755, SN 1999an · constellation Coma Berenices · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A long, thin stream of stars, gas and dust crosses this Hubble image. It is IC 755, a spiral galaxy seen edge-on.

In 1999 a star in IC 755 exploded as a supernova, SN 1999an, found by the Beijing Astronomical Observatory Supernova Survey. Three years later, Hubble studied the region where the explosion happened. Because the galaxy is tilted edge-on, many objects in between blocked the view, making this a difficult target. Even so, the data suggest the star may have been about 20 times the mass of the Sun and around 14 million years old when it exploded.

SN 1999an was a Type II supernova, a dramatic event that ends the life of a massive star. Explosions like this matter for how galaxies evolve. They create many elements and fling them far across space, and their shockwaves stir up material in the galaxy and may trigger new star formation.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.28 x 1.51 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 67,000 × 31,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was made with the Wide Field Camera of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Blue-filter exposures (F435W) are shown in blue, yellow-green (F555W) in green, and near-infrared (F814W) in red.
understand.eye: The red channel is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the exposures of 430 seconds per filter reveal far more than an eye could see.

explore: Galaxies like IC 755 contain billions of stars, and many of them will one day become supernovae, spending their final moments seeding the Universe with new material. The field of view here is 3.3 x 1.5 arcminutes.
alt: A thin, elongated edge-on galaxy crossing the frame, a streak of stars, gas and dust.
